issues.description: Tab key path still hides completion widget without inserting completion
issues.detail: When use_enter_for_completions is False and the user presses Tab, the condition `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is False so the new block is skipped, but the surrounding `if key in (Qt.Key_Return, Qt.Key_Enter, Qt.Key_Tab)` branch will still treat Tab as accept. That's correct, but Enter still falls through to item selection logic above this check on the very first iteration if item is None — verify Enter is intercepted before any selection side effects.

issues.description: Disabled-Enter path forwards event to textedit which may double-insert a newline
issues.detail: The new branch calls self.hide() then self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event). Since the popup likely received the key via event forwarding from the editor, re-dispatching to the textedit can either be a no-op or cause double handling depending on Qt focus. Need to confirm behavior — typically completion popups should accept/ignore the event so Qt routes it naturally, not manually re-send it.

issues.description: New option not added to CONF_VERSION bump / migration
issues.detail: Adding a new key to DEFAULTS in spyder/config/main.py typically requires bumping CONF_VERSION so existing user configs pick up the default. The diff only adds the key; without a version bump, users with cached configs may hit KeyError on get_conf or just never see the option until reset. Verify the config system auto-merges defaults; otherwise this is a regression.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keypress in completion popup
issues.detail: Each keypress in the completion list now does a get_conf lookup across sections. This is minor but the completion popup is on the hot path of typing. Caching the value on show() or on config change signal would be cleaner.

issues.description: Style: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` should be `key != Qt.Key_Tab`
issues.detail: PEP 8 / Spyder style prefers `!=` over `not ==`. Minor readability nit but the project's coding style guide is referenced in the PR template.

issues.description: Tooltip wording could clarify Enter behavior when disabled
issues.detail: The tip says completions are accepted with Tab only, but doesn't tell the user what Enter will do (insert newline / dismiss popup). A one-line clarification would reduce support questions on the linked issue #12728.

review.summary: Small, focused PR adding a config option to disable Enter for completion acceptance. The core change is reasonable but has a few concerns: the keyPressEvent forwarding pattern (`self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event)`) needs validation to ensure no double-handling, and the new config key should be verified against CONF_VERSION/migration behavior. The confpage and layout changes look correct. Minor style and tooltip clarity nits round out the review.
